Subject: Optimizing similarity pipeline — benchmarks & ops next steps

Hi Alyssa / Ravi,

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the success criteria you called out, and the proposed next steps so we all have the same playbook. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Quick recap (pain & context)
- Primary pain: search relevance drop on long-tail SKUs and slow nearest-neighbor lookups during peak promotions.
- Current stack: in-house embedding service (s-encoder v1.2, 1536 dim), nightly bulk ingest into a managed Milvus cluster, Redis used for <1s cold-cache results.
- Scale: ~120M active vectors, avg vector dim 1536, steady-state qps ~120, promotion peak ~700-900 qps for short bursts.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement has an internal goal to keep incremental query cost sub-$0.001 per query for the hot traffic segment.

Success criteria you gave
- Relevance uplift: +6-10% CTR on recommendations A/B vs current baseline
- Latency: p50 < 25ms, p95 < 120ms for single-query traffic; tail under load falls within acceptable degradation (p99 < 400ms)
- Throughput: sustained 800 qps with graceful degradation and fallbacks for >1k qps bursts
- Ops: zero-downtime nightly ingest, ability to replay partial batches, and clear visibility into per-query cost and tokenized pipeline spend

Technical notes from our side
- Redwood can deploy a dedicated serving tier for dense retrieval + reranking. We recommend a two-tier approach:
  1) Hot path: in-memory Milvus or memory-optimized store with KV cache for heavy hitters (Redis or similar)
  2) Cold path: quantized on-disk store (int8/4-bit) to hold the long tail and reduce costs
- Batching patterns: support for micro-batching on inference to reduce per-token cost; we can pipeline 16-32 similarity requests into a single GPU batch for rerankers without hurting your p50 target.
- Fallbacks & routing: automatic region/fallback routing to model-variants if primary pool is at capacity (keeps SLAs intact during promos).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
- Karthik (Redwood): deliver a short benchmark summary and realistic cost projection based on your sample queries (attached) — by Mon 2026-06-22 EOD (attached: initial-benchmark-summary.pdf).
- Alyssa / Ravi (BlueCart): share a 24h sample of peak-hour queries and an anonymized SKU sample for relevance testing — by Tue 2026-06-23. (Ravi mentioned a 20M row export; anything smaller is fine for the first pass).
- Jordan (Redwood): scope a canary plan for a two-week test on a subset of SKUs and draft an Ops playbook for ingest/replay — by Wed 2026-06-24.
- Marissa (Redwood): prepare an A/B eval template for the CTR/precision metrics you called out.

Attachments: initial-benchmark-summary.pdf (stub) and sample-queries.csv (stub).

Would you like us to include an explicit cost/latency sensitivity table (different quantization/batch size combos) in the benchmark doc? I can add that to the Monday deliverable.

Thanks — Karthik

Thanks Karthik — this is a great summary and matches our notes. Two clarifications from our side:

1) Scale: the 120M vector number is accurate for active catalog. The 20M export I mentioned is a filtered set for promotions; we can produce a 1.5M sample for the first relevance pass to speed things up.

2) Latency targets: engineering would feel more comfortable with p95 < 150ms as a practical SLA we can commit to for the first rollout. Is that achievable if we favor slightly larger batch sizes on rerankers?

We’ll upload the sample queries to the Drive link you suggested and I’ll assign Ravi to coordinate the export. Expect the file by Tue EOD.

One ask for the benchmark doc: can you include one row that assumes Milvus + Redis hot cache vs Milvus with an LRU SSD-accelerated cache? We want to see cost/latency tradeoffs explicitly.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alyssa
